title: The Intake Desk
blurb: Every request that hits the desk goes to one of six AI workloads — triage fast, triage right.
hint: Ask what the deliverable actually is: brand-new content from a prompt (generative), autonomous multi-step action with tools (agentic), a judgment or summary about existing text (text analysis), anything that touches spoken audio (speech), a judgment about an image or video frame (computer vision), or a fixed set of structured fields/an index pulled out of documents or mixed content (information extraction).
note: Several requests could sound like two workloads. The tie-break is always the deliverable: new content vs. an autonomous action vs. an analysis of existing text vs. audio in/out vs. a judgment about pixels vs. a structured field set.
traps: A single generated reply with no tool use or follow-up step is generative AI, not agentic AI — agentic AI requires autonomous multi-step action.
Summarization sounds like content creation but is grounded in and constrained by the source document, so the blueprint places it under text analysis, not generative AI.
Extracting fields from audio or video content against a fixed schema is information extraction, not speech — the deliverable is structured data, not a transcript.

zones.name: Generative AI
zones.def: Creating new content — text, images, code, or audio — from a prompt, rather than analyzing or acting on content that already exists.

zones.name: Agentic AI
zones.def: Autonomously planning, using tools, and taking multi-step action toward a goal, going beyond a single stateless response.

zones.name: Text analysis
zones.def: Analyzing written text to surface meaning already present in it — sentiment, key phrases, entities, PII, or a grounded summary — without generating new content.

zones.name: Speech
zones.def: Converting between spoken audio and text, or working directly with audio streams — recognition, synthesis, translation, and diarization.

zones.name: Computer vision
zones.def: Analyzing the visual content of images and video frames — classifying, detecting objects, verifying faces, or reading a scene.

zones.name: Information extraction
zones.def: Pulling a fixed set of structured fields, or a searchable index, out of documents, forms, or mixed-modality content.

items.label: Draft five candidate slogans for a new product from a two-line brief
items.why: Creating new content from a prompt is generative AI — nothing is being analyzed, extracted or spoken.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — generative AI workloads

items.label: Create a photorealistic hero image for a product page from a two-sentence text description of the item and its setting
items.why: Creating an original picture from a written description is the image side of generative AI — there is no existing image being analyzed, which is what would make it computer vision.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — generative AI workloads

items.label: Produce a first draft of a product FAQ page from a bullet-point outline of talking points
items.why: Turning a sparse outline into new prose is content creation from a prompt, the same capability as wl-001's slogans, just applied to a longer document.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — generative AI workloads

items.label: Answer a single one-off customer question in a chat window with one reply, with no follow-up steps or tools invoked
items.why: One stateless response to one prompt is generative AI; the moment a system starts planning steps and calling tools on its own it crosses into agentic AI.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — generative AI workloads

items.label: An assistant that checks inventory, files the reorder, and emails the supplier without step-by-step prompts
items.why: Multi-step autonomous action with tool use is the agentic signature — histack's 'persistent assistant' vs 'one stateless response'.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — agentic AI workloads

items.label: A travel-booking assistant compares fares across three sites, holds a seat, and completes the purchase once the price target is hit, with no human confirming each step
items.why: Comparing, deciding, and executing a purchase end to end with no per-step prompting is the agentic pattern, distinct from a chatbot that only replies.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — agentic AI workloads

items.label: An IT-support assistant triages an incoming ticket, runs a diagnostic script against the affected server, and escalates to a human only if the automated fix fails
items.why: Calling outside tools and then choosing the next step based on the result is what makes this agentic — distinct from a single generated response.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — agentic AI workloads

items.label: A research assistant breaks a broad question into sub-questions, searches multiple sources for each, and stitches the findings into one final report
items.why: Task planning that decomposes a goal into steps, executed end to end, is the exam's task-planning-plus-task-completion definition of agentic AI, not a single generated answer.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — agentic AI workloads

items.label: Scan free-text support tickets and flag any phone numbers or email addresses they contain before the tickets are stored
items.why: PII detection flags sensitive spans inside unstructured text — a text-analysis feature, distinct from information extraction's fixed fields pulled from forms and documents.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — natural language processing workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Language

items.label: A hotel chain wants the recurring subjects in guest reviews surfaced as a brief ranked set of terms, not a condensed prose recap
items.why: Keyword extraction lists the salient terms; the classic trap is reaching for summarization instead, which would produce prose rather than a topic list.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — natural language processing workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Language

items.label: Identify every person name, organization, and location mentioned across a batch of news articles
items.why: Named entity recognition classifies mentions inside running text into people, places and organizations — a text-analysis capability, not extraction against a fixed document schema.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — natural language processing workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Language

items.label: Condense a 40-page policy document into a three-paragraph overview that captures its key points
items.why: Summarization compresses existing text into new but faithful prose — text analysis, not generative AI, because the output is grounded in and constrained by the source document.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — natural language processing workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Language

items.label: Determine who spoke when in a recorded meeting (speaker diarisation)
items.why: Diarisation separates speakers within audio — a speech capability. Trap: it generates nothing, so it is never synthesis.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — speech workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Speech

items.label: A voice agent that must hold natural spoken back-and-forth conversations with minimal delay
items.why: Verbatim Voice Live / gpt-realtime phrasing from the corpus — real-time audio in, audio out.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — speech workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Speech

items.label: Transcribe a batch of uploaded interview recordings once they have all finished uploading, rather than as they are spoken
items.why: Batch transcription processes pre-recorded audio asynchronously — still a speech capability, just the offline sibling of real-time recognition, not a text or extraction task.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — speech workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Speech

items.label: Produce natural-sounding narrated audio for an e-learning module from a written script
items.why: Converting written text into spoken audio is text-to-speech synthesis — the output side of the speech workload, mirroring wl-004's audio-in/audio-out case.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — speech workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Speech

items.label: Return bounding boxes around each vehicle in traffic-camera footage
items.why: Object detection — bounding boxes per object — is computer vision, distinct from whole-image classification.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — computer vision workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Vision

items.label: Verify that the person in front of a login camera is a live human being, not a printed photo or a video replay
items.why: Face liveness detection defends against presentation attacks by analyzing the live camera image — a computer-vision security capability, distinct from face verification's identity match.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — computer vision workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Vision

items.label: Flag every frame of a building-site safety video in which a worker is not wearing a hard hat
items.why: The deliverable is a judgment about what each frame shows, which is visual analysis; the same footage would shift to speech if the deliverable were the spoken transcript, and to information extraction if it were a schema of segments or chapters pulled from the whole video.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — computer vision workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Vision

items.label: Tag an uploaded photo with a single whole-image category such as 'beach' or 'city street', with no per-object locations needed
items.why: Image classification assigns one label to the whole image, unlike wl-005's object detection, which returns per-object bounding boxes — both are computer vision, but distinct techniques.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — computer vision workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Vision

items.label: Pull the invoice number, total, and due date out of thousands of scanned PDFs
items.why: Extracting structured fields from documents and forms is the information-extraction workload — Content Understanding territory in Domain 2.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — information extraction workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Document Intelligence and Content Understanding

items.label: Run AI enrichment skills over thousands of scanned reports and images during indexing so content that was previously unsearchable becomes searchable
items.why: This is knowledge mining — the exam's Azure AI Search definition of using AI skills to surface information from unstructured content into a search index.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — information extraction workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Document Intelligence and Content Understanding

items.label: Return a schema-defined set of fields — call reason, resolution, and follow-up action — from a batch of recorded support calls
items.why: Pulling a fixed business schema out of audio content is Content Understanding's structured extraction; the deliverable is defined fields, not a transcript, which is what would make it speech.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — information extraction workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Document Intelligence and Content Understanding

items.label: Pull key-value pairs and table structure from a mixed batch of contracts, intake forms, and handwritten receipts using one reusable schema
items.why: Structured field and table extraction across varied document types is document intelligence's layout/custom-model territory — the same workload as wl-006's invoices, applied to a broader document mix.
items.citation: AI-901 study guide Task 1.3 (common AI workloads) — information extraction workloads · Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Document Intelligence and Content Understanding
